example.text:
# Example catalog for The Library — a TEMPLATE, not a live catalog.
#
# This file is reference only; the CLI never reads it. Your real catalog lives in
# your shared catalog repo (the one `library init --repo …` points at), typically
# as `library.yaml` at its root. Copy this structure there and
# replace every placeholder (myworkspace / myorg / paths) with your own.

# NOTE — no `default_dirs:` block here, on purpose. Install locations belong to the tool,
# not to a catalog: a `default_dirs:` block inside any catalog is IGNORED, and `doctor`
# warns when it finds one and names the paths actually in force. Override them per machine
# in config.local.yaml instead. (Older catalogs still carry the block harmlessly;
# `library catalog migrate` lifts it into your local config so nothing moves.)
#
# What you get by default: bare `use` installs to ~/.claude/ (global), `use --project` to
# the project-local .claude/, and `use --dir <path>` to anywhere you name.

library:
  skills:
    # Co-located source: the skill lives in this same catalog repo (common for teams).
    # Bitbucket browser URL — https://bitbucket.org/<workspace>/<repo>/src/<branch>/<path>
    - name: example-skill
      description: One-line summary of what the skill does and when to use it.
      source: https://bitbucket.org/myworkspace/agent-library/src/main/skills/example-skill/SKILL.md

    # Source in a separate GitHub repo — https://github.com/<org>/<repo>/blob/<branch>/<path>
    - name: another-skill
      description: A skill hosted in a different GitHub repo than the catalog.
      source: https://github.com/myorg/some-tools/blob/main/skills/another-skill/SKILL.md

    # Typed dependency: deps are fetched first (recursively) when this is installed.
    - name: dependent-skill
      description: Demonstrates a dependency on another catalog entry.
      source: https://bitbucket.org/myworkspace/agent-library/src/main/skills/dependent-skill/SKILL.md
      requires: ["skill:example-skill"]

    # Local filesystem source — this entry belongs in a LOCAL catalog, not in a shared
    # one like this file models. The path resolves on exactly one machine, so a teammate
    # pulling this catalog cannot install it. `library add` refuses a local source when
    # the destination is a remote catalog (--allow-local overrides, and `doctor` then
    # warns about it forever); adding it to a local catalog needs no flag at all.
    # Make your own with: library catalog init ~/dev/my-library/library.yaml
    - name: local-only-skill
      description: A skill referenced by absolute path on one machine.
      source: /Users/you/projects/skills/local-only-skill/SKILL.md

  agents:
    - name: example-agent
      description: An agent definition hosted alongside the catalog.
      source: https://bitbucket.org/myworkspace/agent-library/src/main/agents/example-agent/AGENT.md

  prompts:
    # GitHub raw URL — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<org>/<repo>/<branch>/<path>
    - name: example-prompt
      description: A reusable prompt template.
      source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/myorg/team-prompts/main/prompts/example-prompt.md

# Example catalog for The Library — a TEMPLATE, not a live catalog.
#
# This file is reference only; the CLI never reads it. Your real catalog lives in
# your shared catalog repo (the one `library init --repo …` points at), typically
# as `library.yaml` at its root. Copy this structure there and
# replace every placeholder (myworkspace / myorg / paths) with your own.

# NOTE — no `default_dirs:` block here, on purpose. Install locations belong to the tool,
# not to a catalog: a `default_dirs:` block inside any catalog is IGNORED, and `doctor`
# warns when it finds one and names the paths actually in force. Override them per machine
# in config.local.yaml instead. (Older catalogs still carry the block harmlessly;
# `library catalog migrate` lifts it into your local config so nothing moves.)
#
# What you get by default: bare `use` installs to ~/.claude/ (global), `use --project` to
# the project-local .claude/, and `use --dir <path>` to anywhere you name.

library:
  skills:
    # Co-located source: the skill lives in this same catalog repo (common for teams).
    # Bitbucket browser URL — https://bitbucket.org/<workspace>/<repo>/src/<branch>/<path>
    - name: aaa-first
      description: Golden skill aaa-first
      source: https://github.com/acme/agentics/blob/main/skills/aaa-first/SKILL.md
    - name: example-skill
      description: One-line summary of what the skill does and when to use it.
      source: https://bitbucket.org/myworkspace/agent-library/src/main/skills/example-skill/SKILL.md

    # Source in a separate GitHub repo — https://github.com/<org>/<repo>/blob/<branch>/<path>
    - name: another-skill
      description: A skill hosted in a different GitHub repo than the catalog.
      source: https://github.com/myorg/some-tools/blob/main/skills/another-skill/SKILL.md

    # Typed dependency: deps are fetched first (recursively) when this is installed.
    - name: dependent-skill
      description: Demonstrates a dependency on another catalog entry.
      source: https://bitbucket.org/myworkspace/agent-library/src/main/skills/dependent-skill/SKILL.md
      requires: ["skill:example-skill"]

    # Local filesystem source — this entry belongs in a LOCAL catalog, not in a shared
    # one like this file models. The path resolves on exactly one machine, so a teammate
    # pulling this catalog cannot install it. `library add` refuses a local source when
    # the destination is a remote catalog (--allow-local overrides, and `doctor` then
    # warns about it forever); adding it to a local catalog needs no flag at all.
    # Make your own with: library catalog init ~/dev/my-library/library.yaml
    - name: local-only-skill
      description: A skill referenced by absolute path on one machine.
      source: /Users/you/projects/skills/local-only-skill/SKILL.md

  agents:
    - name: example-agent
      description: An agent definition hosted alongside the catalog.
      source: https://bitbucket.org/myworkspace/agent-library/src/main/agents/example-agent/AGENT.md

  prompts:
    # GitHub raw URL — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<org>/<repo>/<branch>/<path>
    - name: example-prompt
      description: A reusable prompt template.
      source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/myorg/team-prompts/main/prompts/example-prompt.md

# This file is reference only; the CLI never reads it. Your real catalog lives in
# your shared catalog repo (the one `library init --repo …` points at), typically
# as `library.yaml` at its root. Copy this structure there and
# replace every placeholder (myworkspace / myorg / paths) with your own.

# NOTE — no `default_dirs:` block here, on purpose. Install locations belong to the tool,
# not to a catalog: a `default_dirs:` block inside any catalog is IGNORED, and `doctor`
# warns when it finds one and names the paths actually in force. Override them per machine
# in config.local.yaml instead. (Older catalogs still carry the block harmlessly;
# `library catalog migrate` lifts it into your local config so nothing moves.)
#
# What you get by default: bare `use` installs to ~/.claude/ (global), `use --project` to
# the project-local .claude/, and `use --dir <path>` to anywhere you name.

library:
  skills:
    # Co-located source: the skill lives in this same catalog repo (common for teams).
    # Bitbucket browser URL — https://bitbucket.org/<workspace>/<repo>/src/<branch>/<path>
    - name: example-skill
      description: One-line summary of what the skill does and when to use it.
      source: https://bitbucket.org/myworkspace/agent-library/src/main/skills/example-skill/SKILL.md

    # Source in a separate GitHub repo — https://github.com/<org>/<repo>/blob/<branch>/<path>
    - name: another-skill
      description: A skill hosted in a different GitHub repo than the catalog.
      source: https://github.com/myorg/some-tools/blob/main/skills/another-skill/SKILL.md

    # Typed dependency: deps are fetched first (recursively) when this is installed.
    - name: dependent-skill
      description: Demonstrates a dependency on another catalog entry.
      source: https://bitbucket.org/myworkspace/agent-library/src/main/skills/dependent-skill/SKILL.md
      requires: ["skill:example-skill"]

    # Local filesystem source — this entry belongs in a LOCAL catalog, not in a shared
    # one like this file models. The path resolves on exactly one machine, so a teammate
    # pulling this catalog cannot install it. `library add` refuses a local source when
    # the destination is a remote catalog (--allow-local overrides, and `doctor` then
    # warns about it forever); adding it to a local catalog needs no flag at all.
    # Make your own with: library catalog init ~/dev/my-library/library.yaml
    - name: local-only-skill
      description: A skill referenced by absolute path on one machine.
      source: /Users/you/projects/skills/local-only-skill/SKILL.md

  agents:
    - name: example-agent
      description: An agent definition hosted alongside the catalog.
      source: https://bitbucket.org/myworkspace/agent-library/src/main/agents/example-agent/AGENT.md
    - name: EXAMPLE-AGENT
      description: Golden agent EXAMPLE-AGENT
      source: https://github.com/acme/agentics/blob/main/agents/EXAMPLE-AGENT.md

  prompts:
    # GitHub raw URL — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<org>/<repo>/<branch>/<path>
    - name: example-prompt
      description: A reusable prompt template.
      source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/myorg/team-prompts/main/prompts/example-prompt.md
